answer: One tide gauge per identity sits on a ledge shelf, posting a spiral log to a board and locking an 80-credit bond. Auditors recompute each gauge from the tide table: a reading off by over 3 cm, a copied spiral sequence, or a reused key burns the bond. The fee starts at 24 credits, rising 4 per prior gauge by the same funder, so the 1,000th gauge costs 4,020 and 1,000 fakes pay 2,022,000 in fees plus 80,000 locked. A rented-gauge ring fails because a borrowed gauge carries its owner's calibration history, exposed on audit. Honest operators pay 24 once, bond returned after a clean epoch.
